answer: Software farms accounts cheaply, so this network makes every new identity lock a bond only a verified human can reclaim. A thousand sybils must post a thousand frozen bonds. The bond acts as a prism that splits reputation from raw count, so voting weight follows staked value, not headcount. Honest agents keep their collateral crystal clear as steady work unlocks it, while one quarantined account freezes the rest, tying each alias to a shared vine of collateral. Forging a majority costs the full bond per clone plus payloads lost in review, which outweighs one attestation.
